questions.q: Which invoice type represents the ordinary case of an amount owed to a supplier for goods or services rendered?
questions.explain: Standard is the ordinary invoice type for an amount Brightfield owes a supplier.

options: The buying organization, such as Brightfield
questions.explain: A credit memo comes from the supplier, telling the buyer they owe credit.

questions.q: When does a company like Brightfield record a debit memo?
options: Whenever a standard invoice is paid on time
Whenever a purchase order is created
When it believes it's owed credit, but the supplier has not issued a credit memo
questions.explain: A debit memo is recorded by the buyer to claim credit the supplier hasn't formally issued via their own credit memo.

questions.q: What makes a mixed invoice different from a standard invoice?
options: It can only be used for employee reimbursements
It combines both positive and negative line items on a single document
It cannot be matched to a purchase order under any circumstance
It is only used for international suppliers
questions.explain: A mixed invoice includes both positive and negative lines, effectively combining a standard invoice and a credit memo in one document.

questions.q: Which invoice type captures an employee's reimbursable expenses as a payable transaction?
questions.explain: The Expense Report invoice type lets Payables handle employee reimbursements.
